prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. A coherent painted 2D game sprite sheet, genuine transparent alpha background, 1536x1024. Exactly TWO full-body versions of the SAME King Down Pawn, identical pose and proportions, ivory army at left and charcoal army at right, one figure centered in each 768x1024 half. Reference image supplies the exact Pawn identity: charming short stocky armoured foot soldier, oversized closed rounded helmet with vertical eye slits and little pointed finial, small rectangular wooden shield with muted ochre diamond stripe, simple plate boots and tabard. Keep this character, painted illustrated style, not 3D.

New ready pose: body turned three-quarter toward viewer RIGHT, feet planted in a compact braced stance. LEFT image-side hand holds the shield close to the body. The RIGHT image-side arm extends naturally out to the right, elbow slightly bent, ONE gloved hand gripping a straight slim infantry LANCE held approximately HORIZONTAL at chest height, silver pointed head at the far right. No second hand on the lance. Hand remains a coherent closed grip wrapped around the wooden shaft, neutral wrist, normal upper-arm/forearm lengths for this stocky character. Rounded overlapping shoulder armour connects the extended arm to the torso. Arm, hand and weapon clearly visible OUTSIDE the body's right silhouette, minimal overlap with torso. The lance has a short butt behind the fist and a long forward wooden shaft terminating in a silver point; the butt must NOT cross the torso or shield. Keep the lance straight and narrow, no curved shaft, no giant blade. Leave visible empty space around the extended arm and weapon. This pose will animate by rotating the shoulder, so do not hide the shooting arm behind the head.

Composition: each full figure including helmet finial, BOTH COMPLETE boots, shield, arm and full lance tip must fit comfortably inside its own half with at least 35px padding. Frame wide enough for the entire horizontal lance; naturally scale the squat Pawn to fit. No clipped tips or feet, no base, no ground plane, no shadows outside silhouette, no vignette, no haze, no text, no checkerboard, no grid. Top of helmet and soles line up perfectly across both army variants.

Palette: ivory version has warm ivory armour and cloth dominant; charcoal version has graphite/slate armour and cloth dominant with readable painted highlights. Only small muted ochre/gold helmet ridge and shield marking distinguish the Pawn, plus brown wood/leather and small steel spearhead. Match the reference's broad painted shading and crisp transparent silhouette. Preserve the short Pawn identity rather than turning him into a tall realistic adult knight. Two complete matching ready figures, no other poses or detached parts.
